utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the record, up to page 48, line 15, Mr. Stamp never said to which statement of the protected witness he was referring to and possibly what kind of page he is referring to, whether it from -- whether from the transcript or any other page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're now in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovic, now, at 9111 of the transcript, he says in regard to how this unit was formed: "It seems" -- I'll read the entire section just for context. "As far as I know, he, Milanovic, was in contact with Mr. Medic. I don't know whether Mr. Medic initiated that contact or whether he initiated contact with Mr. Medic. In any case, it seems that Mr. Milanovic was allowed to form a combat group so that that group could assist in the defence of the country, to assist in the defence of Kosovo and Metohija. When there were subsequent discussions about groups joining the SAJ, he conveyed that fact to Mr. Djordjevic, and that is how it came about that that combat group was engaged through the Ministry of the Interior and its reserve force." Do you confirm or deny that testimony of Mr. Trajkovic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I totally disagree with what Trajkovic said, and I also disagree with what you said first about how this unit had been formed. This is not about this unit, and what Trajkovic is saying is not corresponding to the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Trajkovic further said it was you who told him about these reserves and their qualifications. At transcript 9090, line 17, he says: "In conversation with Mr. Djordjevic, I learned that these were experienced or partly experienced combatants who had already been at the fronts in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem." Do you confirm or deny that part of Mr. Trajkovic's testimony?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I disagree. First of all, I didn't spend a single day

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) the men that he worked with over there? So these are his various interpretations or various things depending on what he was saying in any particular statement. When it suited him, he would say that he stood by it; when it didn't suit him, then he would say that that was my part and my standing behind it. It's a completely different story. You may hear it if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No -- well, I don't -- we will come to that. So you're saying that Mr. Trajkovic was being untruthful?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he spoke untruth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He testified at transcript 9091 that he wanted to do some checks on the reservists, that he told you that. Do you confirm that or deny that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, please, how can I explain this to you now? In the report that he wrote himself at my request and pursuant to minister's order, it says that those were the men who he knew at the time when they were carrying out those tasks. And then all of a sudden it's up -- I entrusted him with the task of checking up who was capable of shooting or not. I wanted to explain to you, it's not that I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- play any role at all, but it's not the way that Trajkovic is trying to portray it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I apologise to the Court, Your Honour, I called a name which I should not have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Page 51, line 23, should also -- there should also be a redaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you know that many of these Skorpions, these members who were introduced to the SAJ, had criminal records?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are now talking about numerous members of Skorpions. I don't know what you're talking about. I knew nothing about any Skorpions, nor with any criminal activities that they were probably involved in. Can you understand that? As far as I'm concerned, when the reserve forces were sent down there, the Skorpions didn't exist. I knew not of them; I didn't know their names; I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These men that you introduced to the SAJ, according to Witness Vasiljevic he was able, through military intelligence, to learn that many of them had criminal records. Your evidence is that you did not, at the time they were introduced, know that any of them were criminals?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, from the moment when Vasiljevic testified here, a few months later a criminal report was filed against him, or rather, an indictment was issued against him by Croatia for war crimes, for setting up some kind of camps, mistreating of prisoners, and there was an arrest warrant issued for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is not relevant. Mr. Djordjevic, that is merely 7 abuse in that Mr. Vasiljevic – I just reminded you that he said that military 8 intelligence could discover that these -- many of these men were criminals. 9 Is it still your testimony that you were not aware in -- when they were 10 introduced, that some of them were criminals? That can be answered yes or no.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know, and I didn't bring them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Trajkovic also testified at transcript 901 -- sorry, 9102 to 9103 that he's not sure who issued the order for redeployment of the -- of this group of men, but he was informed about their re-engagement through you, through Djordjevic, in mid-April; is that correct, that you informed him about their re-engagement?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this interpretation of yours is incorrect. As far as I can remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is not an interpretation --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- when they were sent back after the first crime -- please let me explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not asking for an explanation just now. I'm saying this is not an interpretation. I read to you what Mr. Trajkovic said, and I just want to know if you accept the truth of it or you say it's not true. He said he was informed about the re-engagement of the Skorpions by you in mid-April.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. Trajkovic insisted that these members of the reserve forces be re-engagement, that he was going to guarantee for their lawful conduct, and thanks to his interest and according to minister's order were sent back to Kosovo. We had a testimony of one of the reservists who was down there who got wounded and who enjoyed all the rights as a reservist. He spoke about not a single crime being committed afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, the witness Stoparic, he testified to no such thing. He testified that many of the men who were involved in the massacre were sent back down to Kosovo with him, except for Cvetan - and this is at page T2844 of the transcript - except for Sasa Cvetan, many of the men who shot the civilians in Podujevo were sent back down, and they were down there many times committing crimes, clearing villages. That's his testimony. Isn't it true that many of the men who were committing crimes were sent back down there, Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let us please focus on a single incident and only one matter. Please do not generalise things. What you're talking is not what Stoparic spoke about this here. He said that they were extremely professional in their conduct when they were sent there for the second time. Well, who was going to be sent back again? It was Trajkovic who directly decided on that because he provided guarantees that these men under his command would act impeccably, that no misdeed or crime were going to be committed. So for those who were supposed or identified as those who committed crimes the first time did not go back again, and it was up to Trajkovic to decide who was going to be sent there or not. It was not me who did that; it wasn't my duty at all, therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, that is not Trajkovic's testimony. Incidentally, was the person we call K92, was he sent back? Was he sent down to Kosovo with them when they were re-activated?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who this 92 is off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could go back into private session just for one moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, he and Trajkovic went after the crime committed in Podujevo to demobilise members of the reserve and returned. And I don't know that he ever went there again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said at page 9709 of the transcript that it was Trajkovic who proposed that K92 go down there with him to demobilise these men. You agreed with this proposition, that is to say that the two of them should try to finish this in the safest possible way, that is to have them return their weapons and to make sure that no incidents occur. How is it that you felt safe enough to accept Mr. Trajkovic's

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I made the same mistake again. This is the last time, I guarantee. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Redaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It seems, based on your evidence, that it was necessary to engage K92 to demobilise these men, to help Trajkovic to demobilise these men. So how is it you could accept Trajkovic's guarantee about their re-activation in Kosovo when K92 was not going down there to help him to control these men?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have made a total construct of this. I told you a few times that the two, Trajkovic and this protected witness, were friends; and they, as it were, committed and carried out a selection of a number of members of the reserve forces. We heard here testimony that only 15 or 20 people with war experience had been engaged. And Trajkovic, therefore, suggested that probably the other man should join him. I told him at the time, All right, go down there, and see that there were no problems in the process. But please understand, that was the period of the fiercest bombing of Serbia. I didn't care much about whether 20 reservists were going to be brought back or not. I have an officer who is in charge of 100 or 200 men with such a proposition. So I really cannot -- couldn't programme each and every step for him. He comes up with a proposition. I say, All right, go there, do it the best possible way. And he carried it out in a professional manner. Later he told me, I need them; I will guarantee for them. I asked him, How many? He said, 100. I obtained an approval from the minister. I engaged the administration in charge of sending the reservists down there. He made the selection. He takes charge. And now you're holding me responsible. All right, I may be responsible, but what I know is that he provided guarantee for their re-engagement. And I know, based on the testimony we heard here from one of the reservists, is that they carried out their job extremely professionally, and they didn't commit any crime. That's all I know. And my role in all that -- and I really don't understand the way you're thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at D442, which may I just say for the record is a copy of P86 with a slight difference in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that you asked Mr. Trajkovic to prepare a report on the orders of the minister. What did he do with this report, having prepared it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report was submitted to me, and I delivered it to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you read it before you submitted it to the minister?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you ask Trajkovic about it or ask him to make any corrections? Did you discuss it with Trajkovic before sending it to the minister?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since at one point he was wounded as well, he wrote this report on the basis of certain information he received from his subordinates down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Djordjevic, discuss it with Mr. Trajkovic before you forwarded it to the minister?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I issued a task to him, the first and the second time when the reservists were engaged for his need, to prepare a report that I was to forward to the minister --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- he brought the report to me. I didn't amend it; I didn't want to amend it; I didn't analyse the contents, how he wrote it, and what he wrote it. I just gave it to the minister as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He says in the first sentence of paragraph 3: "With the approval of the chief of the public security department and the MUP staff in Pristina, 128 reservists were engaged and put on the roster of the SAJ reservists." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was his information. He knows what I had told him, and he didn't know my further activities vis-à-vis minister. When he proposed that he needed the reservists and when he said that there were hundred-odd men that could be used for those purposes, with this request of his I approached the minister, the minister agreed with the procedure, and Trajkovic knows that I told him, after I received an order from the minister, Trajkovic, go ahead and work with the police administration on the issue of reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not sure what your answer is --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, formally speaking -- excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not sure what your answer is. Is that, what I just read, the first sentence that Mr. Trajkovic wrote, is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it was true that I gave him permission to engage these reservists, but only after I had obtained approval. So I couldn't provide this approval myself. Once he came up with this proposal and said that there was so and so many reservists available for MUP, I obtained a permission from the minister, the minister agreed because he knew what tasks lay ahead of the SAJ, that it had been weakened and that it needed assistance. Then I told him, It's all right. See to it to engage more reservists with the police administration. So this is true in the sense how it's written here, but what we have here is his side of the story, his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He said in the fifth paragraph, first sentence: "At about 1800 hours on the 27th of March, 1999, with the approval of the MUP staff and the knowledge of the chief of the department, the commander of the SAJ Belgrade, Zoran Simovic, went to Prolom Banja in order to take over members of the reserve forces that were to be engaged." Is that part true or not true, Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. He was wounded at the time, and he wrote this report based on what he had received from other officers. What they conveyed to him, I don't know. As far as I know about this unit, the only thing is that this unit was headed towards Kosovo, that they were holding some kind of back-up position, and that they could only go to Kosovo if the staff summoned them. When the staff decided that there was a need for their engagement, that was what they decided to do; however, I didn't provide any approval in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, we're not talking about approval here. Focus on what I'm asking and what he wrote here and gave to you. You said in your evidence that you did not know about it. The first time you know they were -- they had joined the SAJ was when they committed the crime. He said that with your knowledge Simovic went down there, take them over. Isn't that true, that with your knowledge Simovic went down there to take them over?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is completely untrue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page, the next-to-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Short paragraph, so I'll just read it. He said: "A need again arose for the engagement of reservists so at the proposal of the SAJ commander, Zivko Trajkovic, and with the approval of the staff in Pristina and the chief of the department, 108 reservists were engaged under the leadership of Slobodan Medic." Is that part true, especially the part referring to your approval being given?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I conveyed it, that those reservists could be engaged for the SAJ. However, I again sought from the minister permission for them to be there. Once I got this permission, I said, Yes, they can be re-engaged. What I practically did was to pass on the minister's approval onwards. Therefore, I didn't have any inherent authority to decide on the engagement of 108 members of the reserve forces for the requirements of the SAJ. I was just an intermediary between the minister and Trajkovic because Trajkovic could not contact the minister directly. The minister took a decision, I conveyed it, and you can, in a way, perceive it as some kind of my approval for their re-engagement, but that happened exclusively on Trajkovic's insistence. It wasn't either my intention or my wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Byrnes testified that in the time that he associated with you in various meetings, you were a professional man, highly professional. A commander, a man who was obviously the commander, and he was speaking especially in regard to -- or vis-à-vis Mr. Lukic. That you were on top of the details, you were a top negotiator, you were a man of substance. Mr. Lukic pretty much said the same thing about you. Mr. Trajkovic came and testified and he said that you were the -- I think he said you were respected in your capacity as chief of the police for Serbia. Indeed, you testified, and we know from other testimony, that after negotiations with General Clark, General Perisic, Mr. Naumann, Mr. Milosevic, you were the one that they insisted on signing the agreement. That is P837. Not even Mr. Perisic signed that one. Everybody who came across you that we hear about first and then second and have a high regard, a high respect for you as a professional commander of the police force, the man in charge of the police force of Serbia. Were you not ultimately responsible for the policemen who were engaged in anti-terrorist operations in Kosovo during the war in 1999, or do you disown them?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this lengthy question, you started from complete falsehoods. As for Shaun Byrnes, he saw me once in his life, and he thinks he also saw me twice, which is not true at all. He only saw me at negotiations, which took place there and that is not in dispute. It wasn’t me who decided to participate in negotiations, no; it was the President of Serbia and the minister of the interior who decided that. I had spent years and years in Kosovo, and what Byrnes said was quite natural. I knew every village, every hamlet, every path and every road, and I knew the circumstances there. But far be it that I was the supreme decision-maker there. Everybody knows who was responsible for what. When I was ordered to take part in negotiations, I did; when I was ordered, Sign this, I signed it. When others were told, Go and do that, they would go and do whatever they were ordered. I am repeating for the umpteenth time, not a single policeman who was engaged in Kosovo in anti-terrorist activities or on the defence of the country, I was not responsible for any one of them, for not a single policeman. Yes, minister could appoint me head of staff, but he would previously need to release me of my duties as chief of SJB so that I could take up additional duties. And in that case, had I been head of staff, then, yes, I would have been down there and I would have told you loud and clear what it is that I was in charge of as head of staff in Kosovo. However, it is quite clearly defined who was responsible for what.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I hear your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that that's the end of the cross-examination. But since we are at the time or beyond the time, I'm wondering if the Court could take the break. I don't have any intentions of continuing, but I would like to formally announce that on resumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 1.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.40 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that conclude your cross-examination, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you indeed. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would like to clarify something that was raised by Mr. Stamp about ranks and positions. So would you please tell me about the relationship of a superior and subordinate. Is it regulated by rank or by position that he holds?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the Ministry of the Interior --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt you. Please follow the transcript so that you make appropriate breaks so that the lady who is interpreting can interpret everything and the court reporter can record it.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Ministry of the Interior, it is the authority of the0 position that counts. So if somebody is chief of the secretariat, regardless of the rank that that person holds, that person is superior to everybody else working there. The same applies to the seat of the ministry, chief of a department is the most important person regardless of the rank that person holds. I can give you two examples. For example, at the time of the appointment to the position of the chief of SUP in Belgrade, Branko Djuric was first lieutenant-colonel, and following that he was a colonel and he was a superior to Sreten Lukic, who was major-general at the time. Also, an example from the crime investigations department. Chief of that administration at the seat of the ministry was a major-general. His deputy was somebody who testified here and was a captain, but he as deputy chief of the administration was superior to all lieutenant-colonels, colonels, or majors who worked in the administration of the crime investigations police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now what about the relationship in a situation where a minister adopts a decision?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When one official adopts a decision or issues an order, it is only he who can withdraw that order or modify it. A subordinate officer cannot issue an order modifying an order that had been previously issued by a superior officer. So I think that that situation is completely clear when it comes to orders issued by officials, senior officials, at the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, please, when it comes to the minister's decision on establishing the staff for suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998, June of that year --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just intervene here. I don't really wish to be suggesting how the re-examination should be conducted, but may I ask that counsel refer to the question or the area that he seeks -- and that is the area from cross-examination that he seeks to clarify, so as to put the question in context and assess if it is legitimate re-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, please carry on. It's clear, I think, that the subject matter as the subject of your present questions have been in a number of respects dealt with in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The reference is page 9769, line 24 and 25; and page 9770, line 1; as well as the following exhibit: P1506 -- no, I apologise, P1507, MFI, which was put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So my question, Mr. Djordjevic, was -- let me just see how I formulated it. Can you tell us, please, given the decision that the minister adopted in June of 1998 on establishing the staff for suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija, were you able to act contrary to that order or issue different orders and tasks that would override that initial order -- decision?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only modifications in relation to an order that was issued could be made by the person who issued the original order, which was the minister. I was not authorised nor was I able to change a single article from that decision or vary it in any way. All of that came under the sole authority of the person issuing the original decision or order, which in this particular case was the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see P1506, please. Could we see the following page, please. Further on, please. Further on, please. B/C/S version we need the presidential decree on decorations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have this presidential decree. Mr. Djordjevic, can you tell us, please, what were the reasons given in the preamble to this presidential decree here for giving decorations?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we've covered this already, but it says here for results achieved in carrying out security-related tasks aimed at suppressing terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija and in defence of the country from the aggression. So the security-related tasks aimed at suppressing terrorists were in 1998 and 1999 and defence of the country from the aggression was in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, can we now turn to the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move it to the right, please, the B/C/S version. No, one page back, please, in the B/C/S. Yes, that's the one. No, no, can you please -- either reduce or scroll down. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we see here the order of the first degree for merit in the field of defence and security. Do you recognise any of the persons listed here as colonels?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know all of them, Maksimovic, Ivan, a colonel, he was engaged in 1998. He had Belgrade detachments under him. Gavranic, Dusan was there in 1999. He was chief of SUP in Gnjilane. Adamovic, Dragutin was chief of Djakovica SUP in 1998, then he retired. Gradimir Zekavica was chief of SUP in Prizren. He retired on the 31st of December, 1998. He was a retiree in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the MFI document P1507. Page 41, please. I think that's in the English version, 41. Could we now scroll down, please. We need the lower part.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In order to be of assistance to those who will be looking at it, the SL initials in black letters, can you tell us, please, this person - and this is Mr. Sreten Lukic - in the interview that he gave, these words of his, to which period of time do they pertain? Do you see what I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here he speaks of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what does it say here in his reply? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Practically from mid-July and all the way up until late September or early October in Pristina in addition to me there were constantly chief of department, Mr. Djordjevic, and Obrad Stevanovic as assistant minister and commander of PJP present.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the previous page -- or rather, Your Honours, I need instructions from you. Should I now ask that this page or this portion of the page also be marked for identification or not? Or is it enough what Mr. Stamp has already done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think this additional page should be marked as well, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misunderstood. It is already part of that which is marked. You haven't gone beyond what is marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. It's on that page, but it wasn't put to Mr. Djordjevic in cross-examination. This portion wasn't put to him, this portion of the page, that's why I'm asking. And I just put it to him. And could we now see page 40, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We can see, now, at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can scroll down just a bit to the end of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, at the bottom of the page, the person who was interviewed -- or rather, tell me, please, what did the person who was interviewed talk about?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He replied to the question that was put to him by saying the staff has -- practically it had -- it has, and that's what the task was, to co-ordinate, plan, and direct organisational units, that is to say secretariats and attached units, number one in suppressing or preventing terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, words of Mr. Adamovic were put to you concerning a meeting that you attended where some sort of a plan was presented in the latter part of July 1998. Can you tell me, please, what plan was discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not -- or rather, no plan was presented at that meeting; rather, they conveyed an order of the minister to the chiefs of secretariats and told them that the global plans for suppression of terrorism had been adopted and that police with its units in co-ordination with the army was tasked -- or rather, would have the task to carry out anti-terrorist actions aimed at unblocking the roads and so on. The officials were told in most general terms that in the following period they would be engaged in implementing the plan -- the global plan on suppression of terrorism; however, the plan was never presented to them. They were simply told, they were informed, that this would be done and that they would work in accordance to other plans that would be developed based on the global plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After this meeting that you referred to just now and that you told us about, did you ever issue any kind of direct order to any police unit concerning their engagement in anti-terrorist activities that had been planned?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that sufficient explanation has been provided as to how plan-based documents were prepared for individual actions; that is to say I did not take part in the adoption of any decision or any order to any unit, any police unit. So all activities of the attached police units and the sent police units, as well as the secretariats, were issued by the staff. It is the staff that planned their activities, issued orders, checked what they were doing, et cetera. I have already explained my role in detail during the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, you told us here that the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit was established as an internal unit of the Ministry of the Interior. Could you please tell us what your responsibility actually was in relation to that unit.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just have to say, as I've already noted, that this unit was related to the police department that I headed in the 1980s. After that, Radovan Stojicic, the commander of that unit, was appointed chief of the RJB, and at the same time he was deputy minister. On that basis, as the former commander of the special unit, he practically linked the unit to himself. After he got killed and after I became acting chief and then chief of the RJB, I continued that tradition, if I can put it that way, vis-à-vis the special unit. That is to say that I had the obligation of having the unit make special proposals to me as the chief in respect of what they needed, primarily in terms of material and financial resources for support in carrying out training. My entire role boiled down to that, as I have already said. The engagement of the units, though, was within the power of the minister. So I as head of the RJB could not engage part of that unit for a particular assignment until a decision on that was made by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever command the SAJ unit in the period of 1998/1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I did not give them any tasks either.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, who decided that the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit should be engaged in Kosovo and Metohija during the course of 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision about that and also about the engagement of other units, that is to say PJPs and the unit for special operations of the state security department, was made by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the engagement of the police units in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and 1999, including the SAJ, who planned the tasks and issued orders to these units?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only the staff that issued orders to them concerning what their tasks would be on the basis of the decision made by the minister related to the establishment of the staff for carrying out anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P1474 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, this is a letter that you sent to "Nedeljni Telegraf" and that the Prosecutor showed you. Mr. Stamp did not let you explain why it was that you wrote this letter.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very often, the media wrote about one and the same events. Things were being written and re-written in terms of what I actually did do up to a degree, but many things were just fabrications. So I decided to explain my role in 1998 and 1999. I was aware of the fact that several years had gone by and that I won't be very specific with regard to certain things, but it's not that I was defending myself before a court of law then. So it's not that I had to explain it in the most precise way possible. I wanted to put things in general terms, but I did not keep silent about my role or my activity in 1998 or 1999. Perhaps there were some imprecisions there or perhaps things that I thought at that moment were not of relevance. But -- well, my wish was in a way to respond to all the things that had been written about me, primarily those that were bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 4 in English and page 3 in B/C/S. If we could just scroll down a bit in the B/C/S and perhaps the English version too. Yes, let's see the bottom as well. No, no. In English it is on the top actually, that particular section.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, can you see the B/C/S version, the second paragraph from the bottom?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something. You said here that the minister had issued a decision, that the public security forces should be commanded and controlled by the PJP commander, Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic, Major-General Sreten Lukic, and Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic. Major-General Sreten Lukic was the Chief of Staff. Could you explain this particular portion of your letter?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence, that is what I said a few moments ago. I said this rather imprecisely, but I did not keep silent about my own role or the role of Obrad Stevanovic. I mentioned that Sreten Lukic was the Chief of Staff. We saw what his obligations were, and in that respect we saw what his role was. And we also saw that it was his obligation to act on orders as he had been ordered by the decision, that is. We also elaborated in detail what my role was and what the role of Obrad Stevanovic was in Kosovo in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you state here that General Stevanovic at the time was the commander of the PJPs.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the imprecision too. He was not the PJP commander; he was assistant minister. He acted on orders from the minister. And previously, he was both commander of the special units and chief of the administration, and that is why the minister decided that he should be there too because he knew the people, he knew the territory. So as there was not a single security-related task that was more important at that time, the minister wanted all of us to be down there and to help out. Practically, in the activities that were being carried out on behalf of the ministry down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have page 6 in English and page 5 in B/C/S now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see the year 1999 over here, Mr. Djordjevic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And now look at the second paragraph where it says "for the head of staff."

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot find that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you see the year 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now look at that paragraph up there -- rather, the second paragraph, not the first one. There is this sentence that starts somewhere around the middle, and it says: "The minister appointed General Sreten Lukic as head of staff."

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And then the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "He also decided that the special police unit in the AP of Kosovo and Metohija be commanded by its commander General Obrad Stevanovic" -- well, that is that imprecision again, the one that deviates from everything else that we have said so far. So it was the staff that was in charge of all the deployed and attached units, the PJPs, the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit, and there was the unit for special operations of the state security department. So again, it's this imprecision of mine in this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1998 while you were in Kosovo and Metohija, did you hear of the existence of a command of the PJPs?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was only the staff that practically planned and organised the work of all the units that had been sent down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear in 1998 of the existence in Pristina of a commander of the PJPs who would be in Pristina and issue orders to those units?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These units were only being issued by the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or rather, could we now have page 7 in English and page 6 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, you have this section about civilian victims in the area of Kosovo and Metohija. Can you find that section?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You say here: "As for civilian victims in the territory of the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija during the time of bombing, I did not know anything." Can you tell us what it was that you wrote about here.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the printed media what was stated was that these were civilian victims from Kosovo that were transferred to the territory of Serbia, that is the story that was bandied about, and that is what I responded to here. And I said that the only crime that I was aware of was the crime in Podujevo. I had been informed about that, and I also knew what the organs in charge did, both vis-à-vis the victims and the perpetrators. That crime was not dealt with by the press, and I was not being accused of anything in that way. So that is all what I said in this respect. By then the proceedings were over in Serbia, and it was a well-known fact who had committed the crime and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now see Exhibit P1226.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, this document which was presented to you by Mr. Stamp and I would only ask you to comment this last paragraph in this report.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last paragraph reads that -- that is to say that the Pristina Corps commander is asking the army commander and says that: "In view of the above, please work out in more detail the engagement of the PrK units in the implementation of the plan." In other words, the commander of the Pristina Corps couldn't act on anyone's orders other than the orders of his superior, which in this case was the 3rd Army commander. For that reason, he's asking him in accordance with the global plan to allow and to provide more precise instructions and guidance on the use of units of the Pristina Corps in the implementation of the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see Exhibit P1227.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness's other microphone be switched on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, what we have here now is another letter sent by the Pristina Corps commander to the 3rd Army command on the 23rd of July, 1998. Can we please look at the second page of this document and the last paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here again we have the same situation in which the Pristina Corps commander is asking approval for the use of units according to the global plan from the 3rd Army commander, i.e., his superior officer. And that was the principle to applied to each and every engagement of units that took place in 1998 as well as the preparation of plans. Everything was based on the general or the global plan; however, for each action the Pristina Corps commander had to obtain approval from his superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now please have Exhibit D323. Mr. Djordjevic, this is a document dated 31st July, 1998, sent by the Pristina Corps commander to the command of the 3rd Army. I'm interested only in the second paragraph of this letter. Please take a look at it and tell us what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the corps commander had certain limitations and restrictions imposed previously by the orders of the 3rd Army command that were in force. Therefore, he is asking for these orders to be modified or rendered invalid, which will more closely define the obligations of the corps. This is another situation that educates how things were working in the army and what was the relationship between the corps and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at Exhibit D424.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, here is a document dated the 1st of August, 1998, sent by the commander of the Pristina Corps from the forward command post of the 3rd Army. Can you please explain to us item 2, last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the 3rd Army had a forward command post in Pristina where the corps commander, General Pavkovic, received from that forward command post precise orders relating to the use of the corps forces. So this is how I perceive this, as another request sent to the 3rd Army, that is to say his request and approval to continue operations against the terrorist forces according to plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at Exhibit D340. Can we please look at page 2 in English and that should also be page 2 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, can you please comment on item 1.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, before you begin your answer, I would like to say that this document is dated the 2nd of October, 1998, which represents an analysis of the implementation of tasks in Kosovo and Metohija and the forward command post of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please, can you now answer my question.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this letter it says that the command of the corps forces engaged in securing the state border and in the area of the IKM, which is the forward command post of the Pristina Corps in Djakovica. I spoke about this earlier, and that means that the use of forces in the vicinity of the border was in charge of this IKM, whereas the command over the entire forces of the army in the area of Kosovo and Metohija, the forward command post of the army in Pristina was in charge since 27th of July. So based on this, I knew that there was an IK M in Pristina as well. According to this letter, the command over the overall forces of the 3rd Army, including the corps forces, the forward command post of the army in Pristina was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now look at page 7 in English and page 6 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, let's look at point 4.3, proposed measures. I'm interested in bullet point number 3, which starts that "Whenever units of the MUP are engaged ..."

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a proposal for measures to be implemented by the IKM of the 3rd Army in Pristina. It says that whenever units of MUP of -- whenever more units of the MUP are engaged together with the army, in the future -- that is to say the army or Pristina Corps, in the future an organ shall be appointed to co-ordinate the activities of all MUP forces. This is a proposal for measures that I'm not familiar with because it was well-known who was responsible for all MUP forces in Kosovo and Metohija. Therefore, I don't understand this proposal for these measures to be undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Djordjevic, we spoke about co-ordinating meetings held during the implementation of the global plan in the summer of 1998. Can you tell me, among the army representatives, who attended these meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These meetings were always attended by the commander of the Pristina Corps, General Pavkovic, and also on a regular basis the then-Colonel Djakovic who later became general. I think that the commander of the 3rd Army attended, but very rarely. I think he only came a few times and the Chief of Staff Lazarevic attended once or twice. It is possible that someone accompanied the army command, but as far as army is concerned, these are the people who attended these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have Exhibit P886, page 132 in English and 137 in B/C/S. Your Honours, can I give the accused a hard copy of this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although the Prosecutor's copy is available as well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need. I have this copy from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So the date here is 21st of October, 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, we see here in the introductory note the absentees. Is your name among them?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who are absent are Minic, Matkovic, and Lukic. So according to this document it seems that I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to page 141 in B/C/S and 135 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, this is now minutes of the meeting of the 22nd October, 1998. Is your name here listed as one of the absentees?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, in the examination-in-chief - and I also think that you mentioned that during the cross-examination - your father died during the October negotiations. Can you tell me exactly when was it that your father died.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the 20th of October, at around 9.00 p.m. is when I received this information. At the time, I was in negotiations relating to these agreements. So on the evening of the 20th he died, and on the 21st of October I transported his body from Belgrade where he died to Vladicin Han, or rather, to our village. On the 22nd we buried him in Vladicin Han. After that, I went back to re-join the negotiations. I think it was on the 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just tell us the year, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at Exhibit P87. We still haven't got the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, what we have here is minutes of the meeting of the operations inter-departmental staff for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. In the preamble, can you tell us when this meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took place on the 29th of October, 1998, at the Beli Dvor palace.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And when was this document compiled? Can you see that in the heading?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the 2nd of November, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 3 in the English version and also in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, you see here at the very bottom we have a -- this underlined title, and then the paragraph right above it. Would you please read it and tell us.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Pursuant to the decision adopted at the 5th Session of the Supreme Defence Council held on the 9th of June, 1998, pursuant to the Law on the Army, the Law on the Defence, and the roles of service of the Yugoslav Army, a plan to suppress terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija was drawn up, which provided for the engagement of units of the Serbian MUP and the Army of Yugoslavia." This is what I have said earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 7 of the English version, the same page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, see here we have item 2, item 1 and item 2. Would you please read and comment on this portion that pertains to good organisation.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Pavkovic speaks here. I think that he briefed on the implementation of the plan, and he says that: "Well-organised co-ordinated action and co-operation between the MUP and VJ units and other factors and organs of authority during the conduct of combat operations." Basically that this entire good organisation and co-ordinated action and co-operation was something that was a feature of the implementation of this plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anybody here in this meeting brief as a head of that co-ordination body, and you were at this meeting. So did anybody do that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. General Pavkovic on behalf of the Pristina Corps gave his briefing and he also did it in the capacity of the author of this plan. He spoke of the implementation of the plan in general terms. And then after him, General Lukic briefed on the obligations of the MUP and some basic indicators of the activities of this staff concerning these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did any of the politicians brief in their capacity as leaders or heads of that co-ordination body?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, there were two or three meetings prior to that and then in this one too. The briefing followed the established routine. Pavkovic for Pristina Corps, Lukic on behalf of the Pristina staff; and if any of the politicians wanted to give any remarks, they could do so, about what was going on down there, about their general observations. But never did they do that as heads of command, as chairman of command, or in any other similar capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P668, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me just inform you that these are the minutes from the meeting of the MUP staff in Pristina on the 28th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 4 of the English version, please. I think that it's page 2 in the Serbian version. Next page of the B/C/S version, please -- no, no, the English version is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the English version, in the second paragraph, we see that minister takes the floor for the second time. And then you have it in the beginning of the third paragraph, Mr. Djordjevic. Just please look at what it says here in that paragraph: Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic: "'We have a plan ...'" and then on.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not attend this meeting, but one can see that Minister Stojiljkovic says "We have a plan." And then he asks the head of the staff whether everything went according to the plan and in co-ordination with the Army of Yugoslavia. This was three days after the beginning of activities, and the minister is inquiring about the co-ordination with the army. He's not inquiring about other matters, just the co-ordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, tell us, please, members of reserve police squads, RPOs, were they on the payroll of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, what tasks did members of the RPO discharged professionally?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were villagers, locals, from that village. So they were farmers and it's possible that some of them held jobs in some companies too. That is to say they had their jobs outside of the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that reserve policemen could also be members of reserve police squads, RPOs. Can you explain this, please.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they could become members of RPOs as locals from that village, as residents of that village. And only in that territory, only for the defence of their village, could they be members of an RPO; just as certain members of the Army of Yugoslavia from that village could also become members of that RPO. But it could be also anybody else, just regular, normal citizens who were not from that -- who were neither members of the police or the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When members of reserve forces were not engaged as such, did they have the status of authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The status of authorised officials and everything that carries with it in terms of entitlements is something that they could get only if they became members of a regular MUP unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When members of reserve forces were not engaged as such and they were members of reserve police squads, RPOs, do they have the same rights as members of regular police structures?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have no rights similar to those that members of the ministry have. They, just like other residents of that village, are engaged in the defence of their village. They have no obligations or rights of MUP authorised officials or anything of that sort. They are simply people who are engaged in the defence of their village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when these persons are engaged in reserve MUP forces, when they're mobilised, in addition to having status of authorised officials, do they -- are they also entitled to other rights as other members of regular MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are entitled to a salary, and they also are entitled to everything else that authorised officials are entitled to when they carry out their regular duties, but only when they're engaged in police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In case of mobilisation, what do members of RPO, reserve police squads, do?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They respond to a call-up issued, be it by the police or by the army, depending on where they are listed as reserve forces members; they go to their respective units; and their engagement in an RPO ceases at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have P1504 -- 1054.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, what we have here is a document of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP which was sent to the ministry staff in Pristina on the 1st of July, 1998. And here in several places, wherever there are item numbers, 1, 2, 3, 4, regardless of the location to which it pertains -- but just read out to us, please, under item 1 what it says here.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Reserve police squad Ibarska Slatina."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us, are police stations mentioned anywhere in this sentence?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to show you this document as an illustration due to the translation into English, where police stations are mentioned [In English] reserve police branch stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could we have P886 once again, please. Page 55 in the English version and page 56 in the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, this portion here, the presentation by Mr. Minic, do you see that? This is the meeting held on the 20th of August, 1998. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Have you found Mr. Minic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you whether you ever received any report in relation to the meetings mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you see where these brackets have been placed?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive a report about the meetings that were held in these villages and what was happening in these villages?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, that's what you mean. No, I never received any minutes or reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From July 1998 up until October 1998, did you receive any report about the activity of the RPOs?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was the staff that dealt with this activity, and it was the staff that ordered what measures should be taken. And they also received reports from secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for reports on the activity of reserve police squads, did you receive them from October 1998 until the end of the war, 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received a single report with regard to this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, in relation to the corpses, did you issue any task to Mr. Bogdan Lipovac?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to the corpses, did you issue any task to Mr. Dragan Pasanovic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I explained here in detail what all the persons were that I contacted in this respect. I explained all of that in great detail here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of any activity of theirs in relation to the corpses?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether and on which basis and upon whose orders they were engaged with regard to these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us the following: During the war, did you attend any meeting with the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, there was this one meeting on the 4th of May. That was the only meeting that I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us where this meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this meeting was held in Tolstojeva -- near Tolstojeva Street because that is where the club of Members of Parliament is. It's a building near that building. I don't know whose building it is. I don't know that to this day or what building, but at any rate on these premises in Tolstojeva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the cross-examination on Friday, Mr. Stamp put a question to you. I don't want to interpret the question, so I'm going to quote it from page 73, lines 23 through 75, and lines 1 through 3 on page 74. Unfortunately I'm working with the working version, the LiveNote. The question is: "Did you not have any knowledge at the time when you planned the defence of the country that there had been a toughening of stances on the part of some persons from the leadership of the country that included expulsion of the Kosovo Albanian population from Kosovo as a solution of the Kosovo problem? Did you not have knowledge of the fact that many persons in the leadership expressed these views?"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have the actual transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please respond to this question.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why I did not answer this question because there was no reason for me not to answer it. It is possible -- well, I remember now that it was probably during that footage of the rally of the Serb Radical Party. I think it was then. And I focused on the question pertaining to the leader of that political party and his speech at the rally of his own party. So I'm not taking into account what that person said in parliament or the meeting of his political party. I did not hear from a single politician of any intention or of any plan or of any activity or of anyone who was supposed to carry out that plan if there was any such thing in relation to the expulsion of Albanians from Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time do you think, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll be very brief, Your Honour, during the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think an opportunity for you to reflect might be useful during the break so that you can be sure you've covered everything. We will adjourn now and resume at 3.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, you told us that, to the best of your knowledge during 1998 and 1999, volunteer units or paramilitary units were not sent to Kosovo and Metohija. Could you please tell us how come you know that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was familiar with the way in which volunteers were sent through the Army of Yugoslavia. Not a single voluntary paramilitary or para-police unit was sent through the police there. I would have known that because the police administration worked with all the police units that were being sent. So had there been any activity in this respect from the level of the ministry, I would have been informed about it through the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that you knew about this because it was the police administration that dealt with that. Tell us, please, for which units did the police administration implement the minister's decision on the engagement of those units?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They worked on logistics and sending the reservists of the PJPs who were engaged in accordance with the minister's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us who decided that you should take part in the October negotiations in 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that several times. It was President Milutinovic and Minister Stojiljkovic who decided that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I put this question to you for today's transcript, so that we would regulate that. Mr. Djordjevic, after the crimes that were committed by the reservists in Podujevo on the 28th of March, 1998, could you please tell me where this unit was returned?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That unit -- immediately after the crime -- or rather, these members of the unit were immediately returned to the locality where they were stationed before they went to the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. This was decided by the staff. So it was in Prolom Banja where the police administration had provided accommodation for them until the staff decided on their attachment to the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Although you've already said this, but is Prolom Banja in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prolom Banja is about 15 or 20 kilometres outside Kosovo, that is to say it's in the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was demobilisation supposed to be carried out, and when was this returned unit -- or rather, when were the members of the reserve force supposed to be returned? Where did Mr. Trajkovic go and the protected witness? I don't want to mention his name.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went -- well, first of all, Trajkovic knew where the unit was and he went there. I think that he first contacted the OUP in that area, and then they carried out the job that they went there to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did they actually go? Tell us what the name of that particular location is.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the OUP of Kursumlija, the department of the interior in Kursumlija, that is to say Kursumlija on whose territory is Prolom Banja as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And after that where did they go?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Kursumlija, after they returned their weapons - I don't know how the services in charge handled this - everyone of them went to their own homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The protected witness, to the best of your knowledge, was he ever in Kosovo and Metohija during the war?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know of him being in Kosovo and Metohija at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would have no further questions for the accused, and I would, in this way, complete my re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You really meant it that you'd be quick, didn't you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, I would like to ask you two questions. One is related to inter-organisational structures in the MUP. We saw several decisions by the minister, signed by the minister, about different topics. If a minister, your minister, signed any decision, who was drafting it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All decisions are drafted by the joint services administration, and they submit that to the minister. As for personnel appointments and as for this particular decision too - I don't know which one you have in mind, actually - but, anyway, these decisions are written up at the appropriate administrations within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And who drafted the decisions you signed, yourself, or on behalf of the -- and with the authority of the minister Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those decisions were also drafted by those administrations. So there would be the basic decision, and then there would be an auxiliary decision from me; and it is these decisions -- these administrations that drafted these decisions, status-related decisions, they would include my signature, and I would in effect sign these decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In those cases, this special unit was drafting decisions for the minister, was it shown to you before it was put to the minister?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The special unit was not drafting any decisions, if that's what you mean. They were not in a position to draft any decisions. They would just send requests to me if they needed some equipment or something. They did not write up any decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps you didn't understand my question or I put it to you in a wrong manner. I would like to know if -- you mentioned the decision, the basic decision, and then were drafted by those administrations, that means by your unit or the state security unit or by -- what do you mean by "those administrations"? Can you explain where is this joint services administration located in the ministry, in the MUP, under which -- under whose authority?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all administrations are in the public security according to the systemisation -- actually, there were a few organisational units outside the RJB, this is the institute for security, the different schools, et cetera. But all the other administrations are within public security. They are fully at the disposal of the minister, and it is the minister who issues orders as to what each and every administration is supposed to prepare and when. But, formally, they are within public security. And there was an assistant minister who was answerable to the minister for these particular matters, say the joint services and other such affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That means a person who is drafting a decision for the minister is member of this joint services administration and then is sending this draft to whom first and then to the minister, or is it going directly to the minister without having reviewed by any other person?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister gives them instructions what to do through his assistant who is in charge of these affairs, and then the decision is given to the minister for signing. If he has any remarks or objections, he then demands it to be amended, whether it be a decision or a letter or anything that he has to sign. So he either signs it immediately or maybe thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said by the responsible assistant. Do you mean assistant minister or assistant?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant minister.
